Rashi on Gittin 23a:10:1.english: And [this is] only when he left [unwritten] - [i.e.,] a deaf-mute, an imbecile, or a minor:

Rashi on Gittin 23a:10:2.hebrew: מקום התורף - וכתב בן דעת את התורף, ולא בעי לאוקמא בשגדול עומד על גביו, ולא לאוקמא כר"מ:
Rashi on Gittin 23a:10:2.english: The place of the toref [essential part] - And a halakhically competent person writes the toref, and [Shmuel] does not need to establish [the Mishnah as referring to a case] where an adult is standing over him, nor to establish it in accordance with [the opinion of] Rabbi Meir:

Rashi on Gittin 23a:11:1.english: It is not Torah - We do not listen to you:

Rashi on Gittin 23a:11:2.hebrew: כאן הודיעך - במשנתינו שזלזלו בכתיבת גיטין, הודיעך שאין שום כח לשמה בכתיבה, אלא בחתימה:
Rashi on Gittin 23a:11:2.english: Here he informs you - In our Mishnah, where they treated the writing of bills of divorce lightly, he informs you that there is no force [to the requirement that it be done] for her sake in the writing, but only in the signing:

Rashi on Gittin 23a:12:1.hebrew: והאמר רבה בר בר חנה - לעיל (גיטין דף כא:) גבי "אין כותבין במחובר", ר' אלעזר היא:
Rashi on Gittin 23a:12:1.english: But didn't Rabbah bar bar Chanah say - Earlier (Gittin 21b), regarding "one may not write [a get] on something attached [to the ground]," [that the Mishnah] is [in accordance with] Rabbi Elazar:

Rashi on Gittin 23a:12:2.english: [They are] Amoraim - [Namely,] Rabbah bar bar Chanah and Rabbi Zerika:

Rashi on Gittin 23a:13:1.hebrew: חוץ מחרש שוטה וקטן כו' - בגמ' מפרש לכולהו:
Rashi on Gittin 23a:13:1.english: Except for a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor, etc. - In the Gemara, it explains all of them:

Rashi on Gittin 23a:14:1.english: A minor received [the bill of divorce] - from the husband's hand to bring it:

Rashi on Gittin 23a:14:2.english: And reached majority - before he delivered it to her:

Rashi on Gittin 23a:16:1.hebrew: דלאו בני דעה נינהו - וגבי שליחות "איש" בעינן, ולא קטן, דשליחות נפקא לן (בקדושין ד' מב.) מ"ויקחו להם איש שה לבית אבות" — אחד לוקח לכולן:
Rashi on Gittin 23a:16:1.english: They are not competent - And with regard to agency, we require "a man," and not a minor, for [the law of] agency is derived (in Kiddushin 42a) from [the verse], "And they shall take for themselves each man a lamb for a father's house" — [meaning] one takes [on behalf] of all of them:

Rashi on Gittin 23a:16:2.hebrew: לאו בר היתירא הוא - דאין להן קידושין ואין גיטין נוהגין בהם, ובמידי דלנפשיה לא חזי, לא מצי למיעבד שליחותא לאחריני:
Rashi on Gittin 23a:16:2.english: He is not subject to [the laws of] permissibility - for they have no [valid] betrothal and bills of divorce do not apply to them; and regarding a matter for which he himself is not eligible, he cannot perform agency for others:

Rashi on Gittin 23a:1:1.hebrew: והוא שהיה גדול עומד על גביו - ואומר לו: "כתוב לצורך פלוני", דקסבר ר"ה מתני' ר"א היא, דבעי כתיבה לשמה. וסיפא, דקאמר "שאין קיום הגט אלא בחותמיו", היינו עדי מסירה, דרוב גיטין נמסרין בפני החותמים; ואמציעתא קאי, ולא ארישא לאכשורי כתיבת חרש בלא גדול על גביו:
Rashi on Gittin 23a:1:1.english: And that is [only] when there was an adult standing over him - and saying to him, "Write [it] for the sake of so-and-so," for Rav Huna holds [that] the Mishnah is [in accordance with] Rabbi Elazar, who requires writing [the get] for her sake. And the latter clause [of the Mishnah], which states, "the ratification of a get is only through its signatories," refers to the witnesses to the delivery, since most bills of divorce are delivered in the presence of the signatories; and it refers to the middle clause, and not to the opening clause to validate the writing of a deaf-mute without an adult [standing] over him:

Rashi on Gittin 23a:20:1.hebrew: הא לא חזר ונשתפה לא - דטעמא משום דעה הוא, וצריך להיות בן דעת לעשות שליחותו:
Rashi on Gittin 23a:20:1.english: But [if] he did not again become competent, [he is] not [qualified] - because the reason is [due to] mental competence, and he must be of sound mind to carry out his agency:

Rashi on Gittin 23a:21:1.hebrew: דיקא נמי - דלגבי פתוח ונסתמא, לא תנא דוקא חזר ונתפתח:
Rashi on Gittin 23a:21:1.english: It is also precise - that regarding a sighted person who became blind, [the Mishnah] did not teach [that he is fit] specifically [if] he regained his sight:

Rashi on Gittin 23a:21:2.hebrew: מדקתני סיפא כו' - אלמא, היכא דטעמא משום דעה הוא, בעינן תחלה וסוף; אבל סומא, לא הוי טעמא משום דעה, ולא בעינן תחילה וסוף אלא תחילה לחודיה, דלא מצי למימר "בפני נכתב"; דאי בסומא נמי דוקא, ניתני "כל שתחילתו וסופו בכשרות":
Rashi on Gittin 23a:21:2.english: From [the fact] that the latter clause teaches, etc. - Thus, where the reason [for disqualification] is due to [lack of] mental competence, we require [competence at both] the beginning and the end; however, [regarding] a blind person, the reason is not due to [lack of] mental competence, and we do not require [sight at both] the beginning and the end, but rather [at] the beginning alone — for [otherwise] he could not say, "It was written in my presence" — for if in [the case of] a blind person as well [regaining sight at the end were] specifically [required], let [the Mishnah] teach, "Anyone whose beginning and end are in fitness":

Rashi on Gittin 23a:22:1.hebrew: מהו שיעשה שליח - לאשה, עבד של כל אדם, מהו שיעשה שליח לאשה בעלמא:
Rashi on Gittin 23a:22:1.english: What is [the law regarding whether] he can be made an agent - for a woman: [Regarding] a slave belonging to any person, can he be made an agent for a woman in general?

Rashi on Gittin 23a:22:2.hebrew: לקבל גט מיד בעלה - ותהא מגורשת בקבלתו, וה"ה נמי להולכה, דכולה חדא טעמא היא, אלא כך היתה השאלה בבית המדרש:
Rashi on Gittin 23a:22:2.english: To receive a bill of divorce from the hand of her husband - and she would be divorced upon his receipt [of it]. And the same applies to delivery [of a bill of divorce] as well, for it is all one reason; rather, this is how the question was [posed] in the study hall:

Rashi on Gittin 23a:22:3.hebrew: מדקפסיל לעובד כוכבים - במתני' בהבאה, ולא תנא עבד:
Rashi on Gittin 23a:22:3.english: From the fact that [it] disqualified an idolater - in the Mishnah regarding bringing [a get], and did not teach [that] a slave [is disqualified]:

Rashi on Gittin 23a:2:1.hebrew: לדעתיה דנפשיה עבד - דהא גדול הוא ויש בו דעת, ואע"פ שזה אומר לו כן, שמא הוא גמר בלבו לשם אחר; אבל קטן אין בו דעת, אלא למה שזה מצווהו:
Rashi on Gittin 23a:2:1.english: He acts based on his own will - For he is an adult and possesses understanding, and even though this [supervisor] tells him [to do] so, perhaps he resolves in his heart [to write it] for someone else; whereas a minor has no understanding [of his own], only [to do] what this [supervisor] commands him:

Rashi on Gittin 23a:3:1.hebrew: לאו מילתא היא דאמרי - מה שאמרתי "אלא מעתה עובד כוכבים וישראל עומד כו'", דהוה ס"ל דפסול; ודאי כשר הוא, ואפילו אין ישראל עומד על גביו. וגבי חרש שוטה וקטן נמי ליתא לדרב הונא, דאע"ג דאין גדול עומד על גביו נמי כשר, דמתני' ר"מ היא, דלא בעי כתיבה לשמה, דדריש "וכתב" דקרא אחתימת עדים:
Rashi on Gittin 23a:3:1.english: What I said is not correct - [That which I said,] "If so, [what about] an idolater with a Jew standing [over him] etc.," for he [Rav Naḥman] had held that [he] is disqualified; [in fact,] he is certainly valid, even when a Jew is not standing over him. And regarding a deaf-mute, an imbecile, and a minor as well, Rav Huna's [ruling] does not apply, for even when an adult is not standing over him, [the bill of divorce] is also valid; for our Mishnah is [in accordance with] Rabbi Meir, who does not require writing [of the bill of divorce] for her sake, as he expounds [the word] "and he writes" of the verse as referring to the signing of the witnesses:

Rashi on Gittin 23a:3:2.hebrew: דמדקפסיל ליה לעובד כוכבים - בסיפא דמתני':
Rashi on Gittin 23a:3:2.english: For from the fact that [the Mishnah] disqualifies an idolater - [this is] in the latter clause of the Mishnah:

Rashi on Gittin 23a:3:3.hebrew: לענין הבאה - לפי שאינו בתורת גיטין וקידושין, ואין אדם נעשה שליח לדבר שאינו שייך בו; וגבי כתיבה שייריה, ש"מ דוקא קתני בהבאה, ובכתיבה כשר, כדקתני טעמא: שאין קיום הגט אלא בחותמיו, ולא איכפת לן אם נכתב שלא לשמה; דאי תנא ושייר, הוי ליה נמי לשיורי בסיפא:
Rashi on Gittin 23a:3:3.english: With regard to bringing - Because [a gentile] is not subject to the laws of bills of divorce and betrothal, and a person cannot become an agent for a matter to which he is not [personally] subject. And regarding writing, [the Tanna] omitted him; conclude from this [that] he specifically taught [his disqualification] with respect to bringing, whereas with respect to writing he is qualified — as [the Mishnah] states the reason: because the ratification of a bill of divorce is only through its signatories, and we are not concerned if it was written not for her sake. For if [the Tanna] taught [some cases] and omitted [others], he would also have omitted [some] in the latter clause:

Rashi on Gittin 23a:4:1.english: That - [baraita] which teaches [that a gentile is] disqualified:

Rashi on Gittin 23a:4:2.hebrew: ר"א היא דאמר עדי מסירה כרתי - וחתימת עדים אינה מן התורה, הילכך "וכתב לה" אכתב הגט, ובעינן כתיבה לשמה:
Rashi on Gittin 23a:4:2.english: It is Rabbi Elazar, who says [that] witnesses of the transmission effect [the divorce] - and the signing of witnesses is not from the Torah; therefore, "and he writes her" [refers] to the writing of the bill of divorce, and we require writing for her sake:

Rashi on Gittin 23a:4:3.hebrew: והא ודאי - כי כתביה עובד כוכבים, לאו לשמה הוא, דעובד כוכבים אדעתא דנפשיה קעביד, ומשום הכי תניא פסול:
Rashi on Gittin 23a:4:3.english: And certainly - When an idolater writes it, it is not for her sake, for an idolater acts according to his own mind, and therefore it is taught [in the baraita that he is] disqualified:

Rashi on Gittin 23a:5:1.hebrew: אמר רב נחמן אומר היה כו' - אתחלתא דמילתא היא, וכן מסתבר, דהא כבר מוקמיה רב נחמן כר"מ, ואית דגרסי "והא ודאי עובד כוכבים כו'" בלשון קושיא, ופרכינן אהא דאמר רב נחמן "עובד כוכבים כשר"; "אמר רב נחמן כו'" תירוצא הוא:
Rashi on Gittin 23a:5:1.english: Rav Nachman said, "[Rabbi Meir] would say," etc. - This is the beginning of a [new] statement, and so it stands to reason, since Rav Nachman has already established [his ruling] in accordance with Rabbi Meir. However, there are those who read [the preceding phrase], "And surely a gentile [acts on his own mind]," etc., as a question, raising an objection against that which Rav Nachman said, "A gentile is valid [to write a bill of divorce]"; [according to that reading,] "Rav Nachman said," etc., is the resolution:

Rashi on Gittin 23a:8:1.hebrew: כשהוא כותבו כאילו כותבו לשמה - הכי משמע: כשהוא כותב קצתו לשמה, כאילו כותבו כולו לשמה; אלמא לשמה בעינן:
Rashi on Gittin 23a:8:1.english: When he writes it, [it is] as though he writes it for her sake - This is what it means: when he writes part of it for her sake, [it is] as though he writes all of it for her sake; thus we require [that it be written] for her sake:

Rashi on Gittin 23a:8:2.english: What, is it not [that] when he writes the toref [essential part] for her sake, [it is] as though he writes the tofes [standard part] for her sake - Since the toref is [the] essential [part]:

Tosafot on Gittin 23a:10:1.hebrew: והוא ששייר מקום התורף - אמאי דאקשי לעיל "והא לאו בני דעה נינהו", אתא לשנויי:
Tosafot on Gittin 23a:10:1.english: And [this is] only when he left the place of the essential part [unwritten] - [Shmuel] comes to answer that which [the Gemara] asked above, "But they are not people of understanding":

Tosafot on Gittin 23a:16:1.hebrew: עובד כוכבים נמי דלאו בר היתרא הוא - הוה מצי למימר משום דבעינן שלוחכם בני ברית, אלא ניחא ליה למימר האי טעמא דשייך אף בעבד:
Tosafot on Gittin 23a:16:1.english: An idolater too, as he is not subject to [the laws of] permission - [The Gemara] could have said [that it is] because we require your agents [to be] members of the covenant, but it preferred to state this reason, which applies also to a slave:

Tosafot on Gittin 23a:16:2.hebrew: ממי נוטלו ולמי נותנו - מכאן משמע דצריך שיכיר השליח שזהו הבעל וזו היא אשתו; ושמא יש לחלק דדוקא סומא שיכול להטעותו, ויש לחוש יותר שמא יטעוהו:
Tosafot on Gittin 23a:16:2.english: From whom he takes it and to whom he gives it - From here it is implied that the agent must recognize that this is the husband and this is his wife; but perhaps one can distinguish, that [this applies] specifically [to] a blind person, whom one can deceive, and there is more reason to be concerned lest they deceive him:

Tosafot on Gittin 23a:20:1.hebrew: הוא הדין אע"ג דלא חזר ונתפתח כו' - והא דאמר ביש נוחלין (ב"ב דף קכח.): "היה יודע לו עדות עד שלא נסתמא ונסתמא, פסול לעדות" — שאני הכא, דגבי גט אפי' אשה נאמנת. תדע, דאפילו סומא מעיקרא קאמר הכא: "אלא סומא אמאי לא":
Tosafot on Gittin 23a:20:1.english: The same is true, that although he did not again become able to see, etc. - And as for that which [the Mishnah] says in [the chapter entitled] Yesh Nochalin (Bava Batra 128a): "If he knew testimony for him before he became blind, and he [then] became blind, he is disqualified from testifying" — here it is different, for regarding a bill of divorce even a woman is believed. Know [that this is so], for here [the Gemara] is even speaking of one who was blind from the start, [as it asked:] "Rather, why not a blind man?":

Tosafot on Gittin 23a:2:1.hebrew: אלא מעתה עובד כוכבים וישראל עומד כו' - פי': בשלמא בלא עומד על גביו ניחא, דקסבר רב נחמן דאיכא היכרא דכותבין לשמה ע"פ הבעל, אבל בעובד כוכבים ליכא היכרא דלשמה בהכי; אבל למאי דאוקמא בגדול עומד על גביו, אפי' עובד כוכבים נמי! אלא ודאי בלא גדול עומד על גביו מיירי, וא"כ הדרא קושיא לדוכתין, דהא לאו בני דעה נינהו:
Tosafot on Gittin 23a:2:1.english: If that is so, an idolater, and a Jew stands, etc. - Meaning: Granted, without [an adult] standing over him it is understandable, for Rav Naḥman holds that there is a reminder that they are writing [it] for her sake at the husband's instruction, whereas for an idolater there is no reminder [to write] for her sake through this. However, according to how [Rav Huna] established [the Mishnah] as [referring to a case where] an adult is standing over him, even an idolater [should] also [be valid]! Rather, [the Mishnah] certainly speaks of [a case] without an adult standing over him; and if so, the difficulty returns to its place, for they are not of sound mind:

Tosafot on Gittin 23a:4:1.hebrew: עובד כוכבים לדעתיה דנפשיה קעביד - תימה לר"י, דבפ' אין מעמידין (ע"ז דף כז.) בעי רבי יהודה מילה לשמה, ואפ"ה קתני: ימול ארמאי, ולא אמר דלדעתיה דנפשיה קא עביד! ואומר ר"י, דהא דאמר דלדעתיה דנפשיה עביד, היינו שעושה סתם, וגבי גט סתם לאו לשמה קאי, כדאמר בריש זבחים (דף ב:), משום דסתם אשה לאו לגירושין עומדת; אבל מילה, סתמא לשמה קיימא, כדאמר בזבחים: סתמן לשמן קיימי:
Tosafot on Gittin 23a:4:1.english: An idolater acts according to his own will - Ri finds this puzzling, for in the chapter [entitled] Ein Ma'amidin (Avodah Zarah 27a), Rabbi Yehudah requires circumcision [to be performed] for its own sake, and even so it teaches [there]: "An Aramean [i.e., a gentile] may circumcise," and it does not say that he acts according to his own will! And Ri says that this which [the Gemara] says that he acts according to his own will means that he acts without specific intent, and regarding a bill of divorce, [an act done] without specific intent does not stand as [done] for her sake, as [the Gemara] says at the beginning of Zevachim (2b), because a woman in general does not stand to be divorced; whereas circumcision, [even when done] without specific intent, stands as [done] for its own sake, as [the Gemara] says in Zevachim: "[When done] without specific intent, they stand as [done] for their own sake":

Tosafot on Gittin 23a:7:1.hebrew: אימא שנחתם שלא לשם אשה - אע"ג דסיפא קתני "יתר על כן" כו', ומוקי לה בגמרא כר"א, מ"מ מה שיכול לדחוק ולהעמיד כר"מ מעמיד, משום דקי"ל דסתם מתני' ר"מ היא. וא"ת: והיכי קאמר "שנחתם"? והא קתני: "כיצד? שמע קול סופרים מקרין", ובגמ' מפרש בסופרים העשויין להתלמד! וי"ל דדרך סופרים לכתוב ולחתום גט כדי להתלמד:
Tosafot on Gittin 23a:7:1.english: Say that it was signed not for the sake of a woman - Even though the latter clause [of that mishna] teaches, "Moreover, etc.," and the Gemara establishes it in accordance with Rabbi Elazar, nevertheless, whatever [the Gemara] can force and establish in accordance with Rabbi Meir, it establishes [thus], because we hold that an anonymous mishna is [in accordance with] Rabbi Meir. And if you ask: How can it say "that it was signed"? Surely it teaches, "How so? [If] he heard the voice of scribes dictating," and in the Gemara it explains [that this refers] to scribes who are [writing] in order to practice! And one can answer that it is the way of scribes to write and to sign a bill of divorce in order to practice:
